direction_name: Papers & Inks, filed: one travel journal, eleven stocks
thesis: Globeskimmers becomes one well-bound travel journal. The binding never changes: the teal banner, the floating tab bar, the three typefaces, one plate shape, one card anatomy and the 16px margins are the same on every screen, so it is always one app. What changes is the paper and the ink. Every Home zone is printed on its own stock and filed under its own tab, stepped dark, light and mid so neighbours separate by lightness, not by hue alone. Every finder is a world of two or three tones (an anchor ink, one accent, one wash) on its own paper, with one quiet motif and one card signature that belong to it alone: a menu leader for Eat, a cup sleeve and a time-aware title for Coffee, a poster band and contour lines for Things to Do. The eleven anchors spread around the hue wheel, the few close neighbours held apart by lightness, and brand teal is kept for the app itself. The profile is the owner's own bound journal in a cloth colour they choose, with the trunk resting on the cover and their circle drawn as orbits of other people's colours. Colour does the separating, so layouts stay quiet; type and one motif carry the adventure, so colour can stay classy. Every text pair in this bible was measured with the WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance formula, and only passing pairs are listed.
principles: One journal, many stocks. Every surface has a paper (its ground), an ink (its words and its one solid button) and at most one accent (the italic word, rules, the motif), plus the shared neutrals ink #16110D, ink-2 #3A3128 and ink-3 #736657. Never a fourth hue on one surface. Stamp red #B0472F (passport moments) and open-green #2E6B4E (status words) are the only guests allowed anywhere.

Colour separates, type unifies. Instrument Serif titles carry exactly one italic word or phrase (marked *like this* in this bible); Inter Tight is for reading; JetBrains Mono is for kickers, counts and dates at 0.12-0.2em tracking; Caveat only on the guestbook doodle line. Sizes are the same on every page and all scale with calc(Npx*var(--fs)), so a new colour never feels like a new app.

Separate by lightness first. Home zones step dark, light and mid so every neighbour differs by at least 9 L* (CIELAB lightness), even when a zone hides. States that must be told apart (intent tiers, restroom access, open or closed, unread) step solid, pale, outline, plain, and always carry a word and an icon.

Eleven finders, eleven anchors. Anchor hues around the wheel (HSL): Bordeaux 346, espresso 22, mustard 41, olive 76, banknote green 140, bluebird 199, lapis 224, cornflower 230, iris 250, night 280, plum 309; every anchor carries a hue. Neighbours sit at least 24 degrees apart, and the three closer pairs are held apart by lightness instead. Espresso and mustard (19 degrees) sit at opposite ends of the lightness scale (L* 12 against 71) and read as brown against yellow. Cornflower shares lapis's LCh hue, 6 degrees from it in HSL and 20 from iris, but it is a mid-tone stock about 30 L* lighter than both (L* 59 against 29 and 29; CIEDE2000 28.1 and 28.9) that carries carbon type where lapis carries cream, so it reads as periwinkle against ultramarine and indigo. Brand teal (175) is held for the app: banner, nav, greeting, links and Local favorites. No finder is teal; the nearest, bluebird, sits 24 degrees away.

Deep inks carry words; bright accents decorate. Text in a world colour on paper or white uses that world's text-safe ink (4.5:1 or better, measured). Bright accents (saffron, ember, terracotta light, lime, lemon, sunflower, brass, gold) never set text on a light ground: they appear as fills behind dark text, as hairlines and icons, and, on their own dark plate, as the italic word or the kicker only where they measure 4.5:1 or better.

One motif and one card signature per world, quiet and drawn from data where possible: a menu leader, a cup ring and sleeve, contour lines and a poster band, porcelain tile and access plaques, a security tint and a receipt, guilloche and the converter, a day arc, a thumb index, accession tags, a lit window, a swing tag. Plate motifs stay at 35% opacity or less and out from under the type (the lit window's single 3px line is the one full-strength mark), aria-hidden, pointer-events none. If you see the motif before the place name, it is too loud.

Stamps print on paper. TypographicStamp, AirportStamp, LandStamp and the commissioned square landmark art sit only on cream #FBF6EC or white. Dark zones and dark plates hold stamps on cream tiles or discs, never on the colour.

One solid per card. The world's Directions is the only solid fill on a result card. The stamp action is a rubber stamp (cream, a dashed stamp-red ring, a stamp-red label), so the passport moment is unmistakable and never reads as a second Directions.

Honest by design. Counts appear only when real; zeros become words ('39 TO COLLECT', 'Your first page is waiting'); freshness is text ('Updated Oct 12'), never a dot; every rating names Google or Globeskimmers; unknowns say 'Not confirmed' or 'Not listed'; thin results get the FallbackDisclaimer printed in the world's own wash.

Emoji-free surfaces. Mastheads, chips, badges, ranks, placeholders and buttons use lucide line icons at 2px (every icon named here ships in the installed lucide-react 0.475). Emoji stay in the tab bar and in people's own words.

Space is the luxury. 16px gutters, 24px zone padding, hairlines instead of boxes inside a zone or a card, three tags at most, one note at a time, one kicker and one title per zone, 44px touch targets everywhere.

word.why: It is the mildest word that still means the people connected to you in both directions, without saying 'friends' or 'followers', and it never sounds like an audience. It sets well as one italic word in Instrument Serif, fits a button and a mono kicker, and it gives the design a shape: the profile draws your circle as orbits, and the mutual follows (the people a private passport is shared with) become your 'inner circle', so the privacy rule finally has a warm name. No proposal made a clearly better case, and all three chose it. The follow mechanics keep their plain verbs (Follow, Follow back, Following, Requested): they are actions, not the name of a group, and renaming them would touch toasts, requests and the data model for no gain in kindness.
alternatives: your crew: warm, but young and casual, and it dates quickly
your company: the most grand-hotel line ('in good company'), but it also means a business, next to Official seals
fellow travelers: accurate, but long in a title, and it suggests strangers on the same trip
your companions: formal, and implies you travel together
kindred / kindred spirits: lovely, but precious on a button
your travel circle: clear, but 'travel' is redundant inside a travel app
your folks: warm, but reads as family and regional

home.ground: Ivory #FFFCF7 is the page. The lobby at the top (greeting, date and place, search) and the closing quote at the bottom sit on it, and in Option B it is also the gutter between boxes. Between them, six zones are printed on their own stocks, stepped by lightness: passport navy (dark, L* 17), airmail (light, 96), kraft (mid, 86), passport cream (light, 97), plum velvet (dark, 17), sage (mid, 87). Option A prints each stock as a full-bleed band, edge to edge, with content on the max-w-md column (720px cap on iPad). Option B prints the same stock as an inset, bordered folder box with a tab. Order, content and colours are identical in A and B; only the containment changes, so the founder compares one thing. Shared text neutrals: ink #16110D, ink-2 #3A3128, ink-3 #736657 (never ink-3 on the mid zones: 3.89:1 on kraft, 4.03:1 on sage).

home.separation: Option A, bands: colour and lightness do the dividing. Bands abut with no gaps and no shadows; each opens with its kicker row (mono, the zone's ink, a hairline to the right edge) and carries one serif title with one italic. The ladder alternates dark, light and mid: ivory 99, navy 17, airmail 96, kraft 86, cream 97, plum 17, sage 87, ivory 99 (L*), so every neighbour differs by at least 9 L*, and still does when the circle zone hides (navy meets kraft, 69) or the shelf hides (cream meets sage, 9.6). Only three edges carry an ornament, each with a meaning: the passport's gold double rule, the circle's airmail chevron, the stamps band's perforation. If hiding a zone ever makes two bands of the same step meet, a 6px ivory seam separates them. Option B, folders: ivory is the gutter; boxes are inset 16px and 20px apart, tab included. Each box has one 1px border a step deeper than its fill and a 28px folder tab in the zone's deep colour, attached above its top edge 16px from the left, so the tabs line up down the page like the dividers of a field guide: navy, airmail blue, umber, stamp red, plum, pine. Radius 18 (22 for the passport and the shelf); only the passport box has a shadow. Both options: inside a zone, hairlines and 12px gaps, never a box inside a box (the cream tiles and white sheets that hold stamps, envelopes and rows are the only paper inside a zone); one kicker and one title per zone; no second explainer card; horizontal rows bleed off the right edge; a zone with nothing honest to show renders nothing. The closing quote sits on ivory under a 40px brass #B8955A rule with a 5px diamond (decorative): the quote in Instrument Serif italic 18px #3A3128 (12.44:1), the author in mono 10px .18em #736657 (5.45:1). Recommendation: B on phones, where the folders keep a 390px column calm and the tabs organize the scroll; A is the bolder magazine and the better choice on iPad, where bands run full width around a 720px column.

profile.concept: Your world, bound. A profile is its owner's travel journal. The cover is the cloth colour they chose; their trunk rests on it (luggage stays on top, as the founder set on 2026-09-30); a bookplate says whose world this is; and below it every part of their world is filed in its own folder on their own paper, using the stocks Home uses so a colour means the same thing everywhere: airmail is your circle, kraft is places, cream is keepsakes, navy is the passport. Their circle is drawn as orbits, each face ringed in that person's own cloth, so you see a constellation of other people's worlds. Visiting someone opens their journal in their cloth; the binding (banner, tab bar, type) stays Globeskimmers, so you always know where you are.

profile.circle: The orbit is the creative followers and following treatment, inside the YOUR CIRCLE folder on airmail #EEF3FA. Inside the folder: Instrument Serif 22px 'Your *circle*' (italic in airmail blue #2B4C8C, 7.49:1) and 'See all' 13px/600 airmail blue at right. Left, a 168px inline SVG: three concentric hairline rings (radius 34, 56 and 78px; 1px in the owner's cloth at 55%, 35% and 20%) around the owner's 44px avatar ringed 2px in their cloth. Up to ten faces, 24px circles with a 2px white ring and then a 1.5px ring in that person's own cloth, sit on the rings: inner ring, your inner circle (you follow each other); middle ring, people you follow; outer ring, people who follow you. Faces are spaced evenly from 12 o'clock, most recent stamp first; overflow shows as a mono '+12' on its ring; a pending request is a dashed empty face on the outer ring. Right, the legend as three 44px tappable rows, each a mono 10px .14em airmail-blue label over an Instrument Serif 22px #16110D figure (16.82:1): 'INNER CIRCLE' 7, 'YOU FOLLOW' 9, 'FOLLOW YOU' 12; each opens the circle screen on that tab, and a row at zero is left out. While loading, the figures show an em dash, never a guess. With nobody yet, the rings stay empty around the owner, with 'Your circle starts with *one*' and an outline button 'Invite someone by text' in airmail blue. No ranking and no counts on other people. Teen accounts see TeenHoldNote in place of the folder. Data: one new profile field, cloth (one of eight keys, default 'harbour'), sent with every face the lists and the feed return.
profile.circle_screen: 'Your circle', a new page registered by hand in src/pages.config.js (key 'Circle'; the file's 'auto-generated' header is stale), opened from the legend rows, 'See all' and Mailbox's 'Your circle · 9' row. Ground: the owner's paper, after the 12px mat. Top: a 112px cloth cover band with a 44px back circle, 'YOUR CIRCLE' in foil mono and Instrument Serif 30px white 'Your *circle*' with the italic in foil. Below it, the orbit at 240px, centred, on an airmail card (radius 18); tapping a face opens that person's world. Then a 44px three-segment control, white with a 1px cloth line, the active segment in cloth with white text: 'Inner circle 7 · You follow 9 · Follow you 12'. A search field, 'Find someone in your circle'. 'WANTS TO FOLLOW YOU' requests come first when there are any: 'Allow' (#2E6B4E with white, 6.31:1) and 'Not now' (paper). The list reads like an address book: A-Z mono dividers, 10px .2em #736657 on a hairline, then 64px white rows, each with a 44px avatar ringed in that person's cloth, the name in Instrument Serif 18px #16110D with their OfficialSeal, and mono 10.5px #736657 '@aiko · JAPAN'. Inner-circle rows carry a mono 'BOTH WAYS' tag with the two-ring mark (two interlocking 12px circles, inline SVG). The action at right follows the relationship: 'Follow back' (solid cloth, white) for someone who follows you, 'Following' (outline) for people you follow, 'Requested' (text) while pending. Tapping 'Following' opens a confirm sheet, 'Unfollow @aiko?', where today one tap on a Mailbox chip unfollows instantly. A row tap visits that person's world; the ••• menu holds Unfollow and Report. Footer: 'Invite someone to your circle'. Within a tab the order is A-Z, never by popularity, and the screen shows nobody's stamp or follower counts.
profile.visiting: Opening someone's profile opens their journal in their cloth. The mat and page take their paper; the cover band takes their cloth, with the foil kicker 'AIKO'S WORLD' and a 44px back circle in place of the pencil. Their trunk rests on the cover, read-only (tap a label for its story). Their bookplate: 'FROM THE TRAVELS OF' / '*Aiko*', handle, country and OfficialSeal tier (gold Honored, burgundy Official, teal House, sunshine Friends & Family), and stats only as far as they share them. One action under the bookplate: 'Follow' (solid in their cloth, white text), which becomes 'Requested' (text) or 'Following' (outline), and 'Inner circle' with the two-ring mark once it is both ways. Their orbit shows the figures and only the faces you both know, captioned '3 in your circle know Aiko', never a list of strangers. ON MY MAP reads as invitations ('Aiko dreams of Kyoto' for a horizon). Their passport opens from the navy door 'Open Aiko's Virtual Passport', where the Blotter (WOW, TAKE ME, BEEN, I WANNA GO, MORE PICS, YUMMY!) prints as small rubber-stamp marks in stamp red on cream, and the guestbook takes signatures, its doodle line the one place Caveat appears. A private passport shows the bookplate and 'This passport is private: just Aiko's inner circle.' Nothing more precise than a city, no edit controls, and the banner, tab bar and type never change. Teen profiles cannot be visited while social is held.
profile.personalisation: In Edit profile the owner chooses one cloth from a row of eight 44px swatches (a fine 2px weave, the name in mono beneath), each paired with its paper: Harbour #284B63 on #ECF1F5 (default), Forest #284A33 on #ECF2EA, Saddle #6B4423 on #F6EFE7, Plum #4F2B57 on #F2ECF4, Slate #3A4652 on #EEF1F4, Ochre #6E4B0E on #F8F0DF, Lapis #263F86 on #EDF0F8, Graphite #2B2F36 on #F0F0F2. Measured: white on cloth 7.85 to 13.44:1; gold foil #E7C877 on cloth 4.83 to 8.27:1, so the foil kicker passes on all eight; cloth as text on its own paper 6.92 to 11.81:1; cloth on cream 7.29 to 12.48:1; ink-3 on each paper 4.80 to 4.92:1. The cloth paints the cover, the bookplate's italic name and frame, the orbit rings, the owner's ring wherever their face appears (other people's orbits, Mailbox and Home envelopes, guestbook signatures), and the segment and Follow buttons on their pages. Excluded on purpose: passport navy (the passport's), brand and House teal, burgundy, gold and sunshine (OfficialSeal tiers), and stamp red. Limits: these eight only, no custom hex, no photo backgrounds, no font or layout changes. Stamps, trunk, items and buddies stay on cream or white; the banner, the tab bar and the finder worlds never take the cloth. Also theirs, as today: photo, name, bio (200 characters), website, favorite places, On the horizon. Trunk skins and sticker placement are earned, never bought. Teen accounts may choose a cloth (it is personal, not social) but have no circle folder and cannot be visited while social is held.

Directly under the masthead, full-bleed, the airmail chevron, 5px: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, #B0472F 0 10px, #FBF6EC 10px 14px, #2B4C8C 14px 24px, #FBF6EC 24px 28px). Claim card, only until claimed: cream #FBF6EC, 1px #EADFC9, radius 16; 'Claim your @username' 14px/700 #16110D (17.40:1); 'It's how your circle finds you, follows you, and sends you postcards.' 13px #3A3128 (11.82:1); the field and a 'Claim' button in airmail blue with white. 'ON YOUR PASSPORT · 2 NEW' in mono airmail blue (7.49:1), then one white sheet, radius 16, with hairline rows: a 28px avatar ringed in the sender's cloth, 'Ben stamped WOW on your Griffith Observatory page' 13px #3A3128 (12.73:1), and the time in mono #736657 (5.57:1). Unread rows sit on #F5F8FC and carry the word 'NEW' in mono stamp red (5.20:1) instead of a red dot (ink-2 11.95:1 and ink-3 5.23:1 on that tint). 'WANTS TO FOLLOW YOU' rows offer 'Allow' (#2E6B4E with white, 6.31:1) and 'Not now' (ivory, ink). The feed, newest first and never ranked, arrives as letters. Stamp news is an envelope: white, radius 14, 1px #C9D6EA, a 3px chevron along its top. Left, the friend's stamp at 64px on a cream square tilted -3 degrees, its corner crossed by a postmark (three 1px wavy lines in airmail blue at 40%, decorative). Right, mono 10px #736657 'AIKO · 2D AGO' beside her 20px avatar ringed in her cloth; Instrument Serif 18px #16110D 'stamped *Griffith Observatory*' (the place is the one italic, replacing today's bold; 'landed at *LAX*' for airports); 'Verified' 11px/600 #2E6B4E (6.31:1) after a 12px dashed-ring check when the visit was verified, never a social tick; mono 'LOS ANGELES · US', and 'FILMED HERE: LA LA LAND' when present. The stamp art needs the feed to send each stamp's id, kind, region and art key; until it does, an airmail-blue postmark ring holding the city stands in. Postcards look like postcards: the 3:2 photo is the front; the back is a cream #FBF6EC panel with the message in Instrument Serif italic 17px #16110D (17.40:1), a 44px cream stamp box printing the place's stamp, a 40px postmark ring (1px #736657) with mono 'LISBON / OCT 9', and the footer mono 'FROM ANA · TO YOU' #736657 (5.18:1). Empty state: a white card, radius 18, a 40px lucide Mailbox in airmail blue in place of the 📬, Instrument Serif 20px 'An empty mailbox, *for now*', the body 'Follow a friend by their @username and their new stamps land here: where they went, when, and whether it's verified.' in #3A3128, and one outline button, 'Invite someone to your circle'. Footer: the 'Following · n' chip cloud, where one tap unfollows instantly, becomes one 56px white row, 'Your circle · 9', with up to five overlapping 24px faces ringed in their cloths and a chevron; it opens the circle screen, where unfollowing asks first. finders.motif: The day arc, inked and sunlit, across the top of the white now card and drawn from real data: an inline SVG dotted half-ellipse, 2px round dots on a 6px pitch (stroke-dasharray 0 6) in Bluebird, at 35% from sunrise to now and 15% for the rest of the day, over a 1px #D6E4ED horizon, with the sunrise and sunset times in mono #736657 at its feet; the dots (1.69:1 at 35%, 1.24:1 at 15%), the horizon (1.29:1) and the halo (1.10:1) are supplementary and exempt from 3:1, because the sunrise and sunset times are printed beneath, the role img label states them, and the ringed sun alone marks now; it is role img, labelled 'Day arc from sunrise at 6:55 AM to sunset at 6:31 PM, the sun past midday'. The sun at the current time is a 12px sunflower #FBDC13 disk in a 22px sunflower halo at 28%; sunflower alone is 1.36:1 on white, so its 1.5px Bluebird ring is what makes it read (5.17:1 against the 28% halo #FEF5BD around it, 4.17:1 against the disk). After sunset the disk becomes a 1.5px Bluebird crescent, and on the midnight plate the lemon italic becomes the moon. The range bars carry the same sky-to-sun scale: linear-gradient(90deg, #9CCDEC 0%, #E3F1F9 42%, #FFEFAA 64%, #FBDC13 100%) pinned to the whole 56px sky-wash #E2F0F9 track (background-size 56px, offset by the bar's start), so a cool day's bar shows sky and a warm day's shows sun, with the numbers always printed. The bar is aria-hidden and supplementary: its fill measures 1.00 to 1.46:1 on the track, exempt from 3:1 only because both numbers are printed. The plate stays flat and motif-free: the saturated sky is the statement. Crest: a Bluebird disc with a sunflower CloudSun (4.17:1).
finders.avoid: A gradient, texture or motif on the day plate: the flat sky is the statement. Lemon or sunflower as text on a light ground (lemon 1.23:1 and sunflower 1.36:1 on white), and white text on either. The sunflower sun without its Bluebird ring. A two-stop blue-to-yellow range bar, which muddies to khaki in the middle. Nudging Bluebird toward cyan: at HSL 199 it already sits only 24 degrees from the brand teal. The orange-to-red sunset card (white on #D4861A 2.90:1) and amber 'UV' text. Emoji weather icons. A boxed card per day. Temperatures told by colour alone.

WORLD.eat replaces CAT.food; keep CAT as an alias until every page has moved. src/components/finder/FinderHeader.jsx becomes the plate and takes worldKey instead of catKey; Things to Do, Money, Weather, Phrases and Culture move onto it too. Motifs are small inline-SVG or CSS components in src/components/finder/motifs/, aria-hidden and pointer-events none. No new dependencies: lucide-react 0.475 already has every icon this bible names, and everything else is CSS gradients, masks and inline SVG. (2) Page. The world's paper is the page ground. Under the banner, a 12px mat in that paper, then the plate. (3) The plate. Inset 16px (it spans the content column on iPad), radius 22, padding 12px 16px 18px, min-height 164px, overflow hidden. Row 1, 44px: the back circle at left, the refresh circle at right (a 44px spacer when the page has no refresh). On dark plates the circles are rgba(255,255,255,.10) with a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.28) border and plateTitle icons; on light plates they are white with a 1px world line and ink icons. Row 2: the kicker, JetBrains Mono 10.5px/600 .16em uppercase in plateKicker, 'NAME · COUNT NEAR YOU', the count only once it is real (never 0, never a placeholder). Row 3: the title, Instrument Serif calc(32px*var(--fs))/1.05 in plateTitle, at most two lines and max-width 72% so the motif never sits under type, with exactly one italic word in plateAccent; a search may rewrite it with the query as the italic. Row 4: the location row, lucide MapPin 14px in plateAccent, the place 13px/600 (truncating), 'Change' 13px underlined with a 44px hit area, and the DistanceUnitToggle (MI/KM) at right as a pill (dark plates: the active segment in plateTitle with plate-colour text; light plates: the active segment in ink with white). The motif stays at 35% opacity or less and out from under the type: most sit in the right third, and those that cover the plate (tile, security tint, weave) are masked to fade under the title. City-level locations add one line under the plate, on the world wash in washInk with a lucide Info: 'Showing places across Los Angeles: {CITY_DISCLAIMER}', replacing today's weather-yellow Lightbulb callout. (4) Below the plate, on the paper, in this order: search (a 48px white field, radius 14, 1px world line, #736657 placeholder at 5.57:1, lucide Search, and a 48px submit square in cta with a ctaInk icon); chips (36px tall with 44px hit areas, radius 10; inactive white with the world line and a #3A3128 13px/600 label; active in the world's ink with white, except coffee (espresso with crema) and convenience (night with lime), plus a 12px X to clear; Open now first; when a world has more than six chips, the utility chips (Open now, Filters, any List | Map) take their own first row and the categories scroll in a second, so Filters never scrolls out of reach; a filter count lives inside its chip as mono 'FILTERS · 2' and hides at zero; no 'All' chip); then an optional mono #736657 result line. (5) The result card. White, radius 16, 1px world line, shadow 0 10px 24px -18px in the world ink at 35%, 12px apart (2-up with 16px gaps on iPad). Photo 16:10 (16:9 for Restrooms and ATMs) or the world's no-photo strip with its motif and lucide icon, never an emoji or a stock image. The number at top left: a plain serif numeral in a 28px white circle, except where the world gives it a shape (coffee's ring, ATM's chip, shopping's swing tag). Then, with 16px padding: the mono kicker (10.5px .12em, world ink); the name in Instrument Serif 24px with a two-line clamp; 'Say it · Translate' as quiet links where the page has them; ONE facts line at 13px, the open state in words ('Open until 1:30 PM' #2E6B4E at 6.31:1, or 'Closed · opens 7 AM' #B0472F at 5.54:1, worded in the place's time zone) · distance · '★ 4.5 (1,910) Google' or 'Globeskimmers' · price; the address 13px #736657; at most three tags (world wash with washInk, or white outline with #3A3128); quiet rows with 18px lucide icons in world ink (Hours, AI DETAILS with the word 'AI' kept, Website, 'Add a photo of what you ordered'); the rubber stamp; and one action row: Directions solid in cta (radius 14, 44px, flex 1), Map and Call as 44px icon buttons (white, 1px world line, world-ink icons), More. The phone number becomes the Call button, not a blue panel. The rubber stamp is identical in every world wherever the place is stampable: full width, 48px, radius 14, cream #FBF6EC, a 1.5px dashed #B0472F ring inset 3px like a stamp's perforation, a lucide Stamp, and 'I was here, get the stamp' 15px/700 #B0472F (5.15:1), with 'Only at the place, by GPS · How stamps work' 12px #736657 (5.57:1 on white) beneath. It is never a solid fill, so a card has exactly one solid button. (6) Honest states, restyled only by tokens: the FallbackDisclaimer on the world wash in washInk with a lucide Info ('Only 3 places nearby match, so we widened the search to 25 mi'); 'Updated Oct 12' as text; every rating's source named; 'Not confirmed' or 'Not listed' for unknowns; FinderEmptyState on white with a 32px lucide icon in world ink, an Instrument Serif 20px line, a 13px #3A3128 hint and one 'Expand radius' outline button in world ink that steps +5 mi up to the 25-mile ceiling; skeletons in the world wash, never blue-grey; Back-to-top a 44px circle in the world ink with a white arrow, 12px above the nav. (7) Spacing and type: 16px gutters, 12px between cards, 28px between sections, and the same three faces and sizes on all eleven pages. What varies by world: the paper, the plate, the accent, the wash, one motif, one card signature, the title words, the number's shape and the tag vocabulary. Nothing else.
banner_and_nav: Both stay exactly as built and identical on every screen, untouched by any world, zone or cloth. BrandBanner: calc(50px + env(safe-area-inset-top)), linear-gradient(135deg, #0E8077 0%, #14B5A6 60%, #2DD4BF 100%), the white Inter Tight 800 15.5px 'Globeskimmers' wordmark and its soft teal shadow. White measures 2.56 to 2.83:1 on the mid-teal; WCAG 1.4.3 exempts logotypes, so the gradient stays (Papers & Inks' proposed regradient is not adopted) and nothing else may ever put text on it. The eyeglass text-size button sits at the banner's right on every screen, now including Home. Every page starts with a 12px mat in its own ground under the banner, so the teal never butts against Bordeaux, espresso, lapis or a cloth. FloatingNav: the dark pill rgba(22,17,13,.92) with its blur, 22px above the bottom safe area, five tabs (Home, Mailbox, Passport, Profile, Settings) as emoji plus label in #FAF7EE, the active tab on the teal gradient; finder pages highlight no tab; Mailbox keeps its unread dot (an alert, not a freshness dot). One addition: an always-on 1px rgba(251,246,236,.12) outer ring, so the pill's edge still reads when it floats over the navy or plum Home bands and the dark plates. Every page reserves calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) at the bottom so the last card clears the pill, and Back-to-top sits 12px above the pill, never over it.
